picks.title: Reflector is a FREE open-source sample discovery workstation for macOS
picks.rationale: Free open-source ML tool that indexes your own library by harmonic relationship — changes how a producer digs for samples tomorrow, with zero generative baggage.
picks.excerpt: Austin Rockman's free, open-source Reflector analyses your own sample library locally with machine learning and lets you browse it by harmonic relationship rather than folder names. It is generative-free AI for producers: the model finds what you already own instead of inventing new audio.

picks.title: Dreamtonics tease upcoming release: 'human nuance is not a switch'
picks.rationale: The Synthesizer V / Vocoflex studio signals its next move is expressive control of AI vocals, not one-click replacement — the most-watched vocal-synthesis roadmap in the DAW world.
picks.excerpt: Dreamtonics — the studio behind Synthesizer V Studio and the real-time voice-morphing plug-in Vocoflex — has teased a new product with a single line: 'human nuance is not a switch.' The tease points at the next step in AI vocal synthesis being about expressive control rather than one-click replacement.

picks.title: The Music Industry Is Trying to Guess the AI Recipe After Dinner Was Served
picks.rationale: Argues detection is the wrong fight and provenance must be captured in the session — with TIDAL already gating royalties on AI labels, session metadata becomes money.
picks.excerpt: An op-ed arguing the industry is obsessing over AI detection — guessing the recipe after dinner is served — when what creators need is provenance captured while the work is being made. With TIDAL already using AI labels to gate royalties, 'metadata becomes money' and the credit trail has to start in the session, not the audit.

picks.title: Daft Punk's Thomas Bangalter: 'I'm not really interested in the creative usage of AI'
picks.rationale: A precise craft critique of prompt-driven tools — creation forced through language — from electronic music's most machine-literate artist; the counterweight to the text-to-music narrative.
picks.excerpt: Thomas Bangalter says he is 'not really interested in the creative usage of artificial intelligence', arguing that prompt-driven tools force creation through language while his own process happens at a level that 'does not express itself through words'. A pointed craft critique of text-to-music from one of electronic music's most machine-literate artists.

picks.title: Two class action lawsuits filed over Suno's big data breach
picks.rationale: 55.3 million exposed accounts turns the AI tool sitting inside your workflow into a data-risk question — projects and personal data, not just copyright.
picks.excerpt: Two class actions have been filed over the breach that exposed data tied to 55.3 million Suno accounts, alleging 'negligent and/or reckless' storage. A reminder that the AI tools now sitting inside music workflows also hold creators' projects and personal data.
